column1: # The intended differences between the bash Jig and a port (tests/lib/parity.sh check).
# One entry per line, five fields separated by TAB:
#   <port>  <calls>  <view>  <lines>  <reason>
#   port    the port's name (--name; by default the basename of --port), or * for every port
#   calls   a shell glob over <file>/<test>/<NNNN>, e.g. context/*/*
#   view    exit, stdout, stderr, changes, git.after, files/<glob> (the normalised path
#           after files/, e.g. files/_T_/repo/.ai/x, the
#           NTFS-safe name of format 2) or * for any view
#   lines   an extended regular expression: the difference is intended only when EVERY
#           changed line of the diff (the - and + lines, without their sign and without
#           the --- and +++ headers) matches it; - stands for any lines. For the view
#           exit the text matched is `<bash exit> -> <port exit>`.
#   reason  why the difference is intended; required, never empty
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. An entry whose port and calls fit a
# compared call in a run but which covers no difference is stale and fails the run.
# A wrong field count or an empty reason is a usage error (exit 2) that names file:line.
# jig context (tasks pilot-context-go, pilot-context-ts).
# bash leaves its temporary rows and id-map files behind in TMPDIR when resolve dies (jig_die ends the
# shell before its rm runs); their names carry the pid, so even bash differs from its own recording.

column1: # A pause honoured at the stage boundary: bash runs `task pause --if-requested`, which runs `queue cancel`, as
# nested jig processes, each recording itself as this checkout's last command; a port pauses in-process
# (spec stack-migration: no mixed code), so the records keep the command the person ran.
go
column4: ^command: (queue cancel task:t1 pause --json|context resolve --task t1 --stage implement --files x)$
column5: the checkout records the command that was run, not the last nested jig process bash started to pause the task
